title: Type Checker Internals
concept: The type checker validates type correctness and infers types — ensuring Int doesn't flow into Str, and resolving generic types at compile time.
why: Type errors are the most common compiler errors. Understanding the type checker helps you write code that compiles on first try and debug type mismatches quickly.
tips: Type inference reduces boilerplate — let the compiler figure out types when obvious
Unification is the core algorithm — it works like solving equations: T1 = T2, T2 = Int, therefore T1 = Int
The type checker works ONE module at a time — cross-module types are resolved via interface files
Read type errors from the first mention — it's usually the root cause
common_mistakes: Assuming type inference works for all cases — complex generic code may need annotations
Ignoring 'type annotations needed' errors — adding types improves both compilation and readability
Creating type checking cycles — TypeA has field TypeB, TypeB has field TypeA (use Box or reference)
